skill.name: check-plan
skill.description: Audit implementation progress against a plan, compare changed files to requirements, verify removals, and produce remaining work and validation status.
skill.summary: Checks whether planned coding work is complete and ready for review.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and example report text, not executable Ruby shell backticks. I confirmed the GitHub CLI lookup and validation command blocks as medium-risk operational commands because they can use network access or execute project-defined scripts. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Validation commands can execute project code.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before running npm scripts, TypeScript, ESLint, or build commands, especially in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI issue lookup uses network access and local credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Only run gh issue view after user approval, and allow the user to provide issue text directly.

remediation.issue: Generic shell snippets may be translated into unsafe commands.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer tool APIs or safely quoted arguments for searches and file checks when converting examples into commands.

content.value_statement: Implementation plans often drift from the finished code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured audit of progress, gaps, removals, and validation status.
actual_capabilities: Identifies a plan file and maps affected files to plan items.
Reviews git status, diffs, and recent commits when available.
Checks planned removals against current code and flags missing removals.
Compares original issue requirements with implemented work.
Builds progress reports with completion status, quality issues, and remaining tasks.
Prompts validation with typecheck, lint, and build commands when applicable.
limitations: It depends on access to the plan, repository files, and original issue context.
Validation commands may execute project scripts and should be approved for untrusted repositories.
It cannot prove runtime behavior without tests or a working local environment.
It may need user guidance when multiple plans or issues match the work.

use_cases.title: Pre-review plan audit
use_cases.description: Check whether implementation matches the plan before opening or updating a review request.

use_cases.title: Release readiness check
use_cases.description: Confirm that planned work, removals, quality checks, and validation tasks are complete before release.

use_cases.title: Interrupted work recovery
use_cases.description: Rebuild a clear task list after work paused across commits, branches, or contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Check my current plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the current implementation against the relevant plan. Tell me what is done, partial, not started, and what I should do next.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a specific plan file
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused audit with a known plan path
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the check-plan skill on .plans/my-plan.todo.md. Compare the plan to the current repository and produce a progress report.

prompt_templates.title: Verify removals and validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Review before marking a plan complete
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the plan with special attention to the removal spec, typecheck status, lint status, build status, and remaining quality issues.

prompt_templates.title: Compare issue coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether the implementation satisfies the original issue requirements, not only the plan steps. Identify any missing acceptance criteria or plan gaps.

output_examples.input: Check whether my authentication refactor plan is complete.
output_examples.output: A progress report with overall completion, completed steps, partial work, missing removals, validation results, and ordered next actions.

output_examples.input: Verify that the cleanup plan can move from todo to done.
output_examples.output: A readiness assessment that highlights remaining old code, quality concerns, failed checks, and whether the plan meets completion criteria.

output_examples.input: Find what is left after a teammate implemented part of this plan.
output_examples.output: A file-by-file audit that maps changed files to plan items and produces a practical remaining task list.

best_practices: Provide the plan path, branch context, and original issue link when available.
Let the assistant inspect changed files and diffs before judging completion.
Approve validation commands only after confirming the repository is trusted.
anti_patterns: Do not mark a plan complete only because files changed.
Do not skip original issue requirements when checking plan completion.
Do not run validation scripts from repositories you do not trust.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It compares a plan, changed files, removals, original requirements, and validation status to judge implementation progress.

faq.question: Does it edit my code?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for audit work. It may propose reports and task lists, but code changes should be separate user-approved work.

faq.question: Can it run validation commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests typecheck, lint, and build commands when applicable, but these should be approved in untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Does it require a plan file?
faq.answer: It works best with a plan file. If no plan is clear, the assistant should ask which plan to check.

faq.question: Can it compare against the original issue?
faq.answer: Yes. It explicitly checks original requirements so plan gaps are not hidden by completed plan steps.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It fits engineers, leads, and maintainers who need evidence-based progress checks before review or release.
